capture: pass-through CONNECT observation; destination host, port, tunnel count and coarse outcome only

phases.description: Authenticated launch: token exchange, one automatically-selected model turn, and one read-only shell tool call, on a fixed --session-id.

destinations.role: model traffic (CAPI host assigned to this account by the token exchange)
telemetry; contacted here, and shown by the pack-only-wall phase to be losable without failing a session

phases.description: Resume of the same session by exact id, with one further automatically-selected model turn.

destinations.role: control plane (/copilot_internal token exchange, repeated per launch)

phases.description: The sufficiency phase: only destinations the released net-github-copilot pack names were dialable, everything else refused exactly as a filtered launch would refuse it. A full turn plus a read-only shell tool call still completed, with telemetry refused.

destinations.role: telemetry, refused by the pack-only wall; the session completed anyway, which is what makes leaving it out of the pack an observation rather than an assumption

evidenceGaps: Token refresh was not observed: every session was far shorter than a token lifetime, and forcing a refresh would have meant manipulating the account.
Managed settings and content exclusion were not exercised, so no destination is claimed for them beyond the control-plane host they share with the token exchange.

Business and enterprise plan tiers were not observed. The CAPI host is assigned per account at token exchange, so other tiers are expected to use other hosts; none is authored here, and such a launch stays denied.
Linux only. No macOS run was captured, so a platform-specific route difference would not have been seen.
MCP servers, web tools and `gh` were not exercised; they are separate features with their own destinations.
